content.title: Online Gambling: An Easy Way to Make Money or a Silent Trap of Destruction?
content.subtitle: The Devastating Reality of Ruined Youth and How to Safeguard Your Family
content.body:
Double your money with one click; become a millionaire through a few seconds of prediction. Lured by such flashy social media advertisements, millions of students and young people are losing their way. Dreaming of becoming rich overnight with little effort, they are falling into the dark abyss of online gambling and betting. What begins as curiosity or casual entertainment quickly becomes an uncontrollable addiction, draining family savings, destroying households, and sometimes pushing young people toward suicide.

The Silent Spread of Gambling in Every Home Through Technology

Gambling once meant secret gatherings in dark alleys or around fairgrounds. Today, its poisonous grip has reached our fingertips through smartphone screens. Online casinos, sports betting apps, and so-called 'earning games' are emerging around the IPL, BPL, and major football tournaments. Some irresponsible social media influencers promote these destructive platforms for money, misleading young people. Teenagers and young adults are losing their tuition fees, semester expenses, and even money borrowed from friends at high interest.

Tragedies in the News: Names, Places, and Real Stories

Reports in newspapers and on social media reveal the heartbreaking reality of families devastated by online gambling. These are not fictional stories but brutal realities of our society:

  • Kalabagan, Dhaka: Mohammad Faisal Mahmud, a 21-year-old student at a technical college in Narayanganj, was addicted to online gambling. After failing to arrange money for gambling, he argued with his mother. Overwhelmed by despair, he died by suicide after jumping from the 13th floor of a building in Kalabagan.

  • Homna, Cumilla: Merajul Islam, a 44-year-old expatriate who had worked in Oman, returned home and lost all his savings, around BDT 2.2 million, to online gambling within just 15 days. Unable to face people after losing everything, he died by suicide after consuming poisonous tablets, leaving behind his wife and four young children.

  • Barura, Cumilla: Following a dispute over money transactions through an online betting app, Rakib Hossain, a 16-year-old student from Deora village, was brutally attacked by his friends. After fighting for his life in the hospital ICU for four days, he passed away.

Across the country, reports of people holding families hostage over unpaid debts, selling ancestral homes, and turning to crimes like theft are becoming increasingly common.

The Mirage of Haram Earnings and the Emptiness of the Hereafter

Islam explicitly declares gambling and lotteries impure acts of Satan (Rijs) and strictly prohibits them. Allah warns in the Holy Quran that Satan seeks to create hostility and hatred through gambling and intoxicants and turn people away from His remembrance and Salah. Money gained without lawful trade or honest effort, by taking another person's rights through a game of chance, can never bring blessings into a home. This mirage of haram earnings destroys a person's dignity, ruins families, and puts the Hereafter at risk.

Protecting Families and Finding a Way Out

We must act now to protect our families and future generations from this destructive epidemic:

  • Monitor Behaviour and Financial Habits: Notice whether your child is becoming withdrawn, losing interest in studies, or repeatedly demanding unusually large amounts of money.

  • Build Trust and Encourage Open Communication: Create a friendly environment where children can openly tell their parents about online temptations or dangers without fear.

  • Teach Hard Work and Halal Earnings: Instil the Islamic values of contentment and earning through honest effort from an early age.

  • Digital Protection at the Network Level: Simply deleting an app is not enough. Use modern firewall or filtering systems to block gambling, betting, and inappropriate websites through your home's Wi-Fi and internet connection.

Now is the time to protect your children and family. Break free from the illusion of getting rich easily and build a halal, safe, and blessed future.
